questions.question: At which location on the Earth's surface would a standard object experience the maximum acceleration due to gravity g ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Poles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acceleration due to gravity (**g**) is the acceleration gained by an object due to the **gravitational force** of the Earth. Its value on the surface of the Earth is determined by the formula **g = GM / R²**, where **G** is the universal gravitational constant, **M** is the mass of the Earth, and **R** is the radius of the Earth.
 
• The Earth is not a perfect sphere but an **oblate spheroid**, meaning it is flattened at the **Poles** and bulges at the **Equator**. This shape is caused by the Earth's **rotation**.
 
• Because of this shape, the **equatorial radius** (approximately **6,378 km**) is about **21 km** longer than the **polar radius** (approximately **6,357 km**).
 
• Since the value of **g** is **inversely proportional** to the square of the distance from the center of the Earth (**R**), the value of **g** is highest where the radius is the smallest. Therefore, **g** is maximum at the **Poles**.
 
• Quantitatively, the value of **g** at the **Poles** is approximately **9.832 m/s²**, which is greater than the value at the **Equator**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Effect of Rotation (Centrifugal Force):** The rotation of the Earth creates a **centrifugal force** that acts outward, away from the Earth's axis. This force is strongest at the **Equator** and zero at the **Poles**. This outward force partially counteracts the pull of gravity, further reducing the effective value of **g** at the **Equator**.
 
• **The Equator:** At the **Equator** (**0 degrees latitude**), the combination of the maximum radius and the maximum centrifugal force results in the **minimum** value of acceleration due to gravity, which is approximately **9.780 m/s²**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Tropics:** The **Tropic of Cancer** (**23.5 degrees North**) and the **Tropic of Capricorn** (**23.5 degrees South**) are located at intermediate latitudes. The value of **g** at these locations is higher than at the **Equator** but significantly lower than at the **Poles**. ***Hence, options 2 and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:** While the **mass** of an object remains **constant** regardless of location, its **weight** (**W = mg**) changes. An object will weigh the most at the **Poles** and the least at the **Equator** because of the variation in **g**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Variation with Altitude:** As one moves higher above the Earth's surface (increasing **altitude**), the value of **g** decreases because the distance from the center of the Earth increases.
 
• **Variation with Depth:** If one goes below the surface of the Earth (increasing **depth**), the value of **g** also **decreases**. This is because the mass of the Earth contributing to the gravitational pull decreases. At the **Center of the Earth**, the value of **g** becomes **zero**.
 
• **Standard Gravity:** For most physics calculations, a **standard gravity** value of **9.80665 m/s²** is used, which represents an average value at **45 degrees latitude** at sea level.
 
• **Gravitational Constant:** The value of **G** is **6.674 x 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²**, which was first measured by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**.

3

Why do we spread cloths while putting them for drying in open sky?

a. Increasing the surface area will increase the rate of evaporation
b. Increase in wind speed will not allow the cloth to fly
c. To remove wrinkles
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary reason for spreading clothes in the open sky is that **increasing the surface area** directly leads to an **increase in the rate of evaporation**. Since evaporation is a **surface phenomenon**, a larger area allows more water molecules to acquire enough **kinetic energy** to escape into the atmosphere simultaneously. ***Hence, statement a is correct.***
 
• Spreading the cloth actually increases its **air resistance**, making it more likely to be carried away by a strong breeze if not secured. The claim that it prevents the cloth from flying due to wind speed is logically and physically inconsistent with the act of spreading. ***Hence, statement b is incorrect.***
 
• While spreading clothes may help in reducing **wrinkles** or **creases** as they dry, it is a secondary aesthetic benefit and not the fundamental physical reason related to the efficiency of the **drying process** in the open sky. ***Hence, statement c is incorrect.***
 
• In the context of **physics** and **thermal properties**, the time taken for a liquid to change into **vapor** at a temperature below its **boiling point** is minimized when the liquid is spread over a **maximum area**.
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Only a.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• It is the process by which **water** changes from a **liquid** to a **gas** or **vapor**. It is a vital part of the **water cycle** and occurs at all temperatures, unlike boiling which occurs at a **fixed temperature** (e.g., **100 degrees Celsius** for water at sea level).
 
• Energy in the form of **heat** (often from the **Sun**) is required to break the molecular bonds of the liquid.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting the Rate of Evaporation:**
 
 
• **Surface Area:** As seen in this example, a larger **exposed area** facilitates faster **vaporization** because more particles are at the surface.
 
• **Temperature:** An increase in **ambient temperature** provides more **heat energy** to the water molecules, increasing their **velocity** and the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Humidity:** The rate of evaporation is **inversely proportional** to the **humidity** of the surrounding air. If the air is already saturated with **water vapor**, the drying process slows down significantly.
 
• **Wind Speed:** Higher **wind speeds** help move the saturated air away from the surface of the wet cloth, replacing it with **dry air**, which accelerates the process.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• This principle is used in **cooling towers**, **salt production** (from seawater in large shallow ponds), and even in the **biological cooling** mechanism of **sweating** in humans.

questions.question: Select the correct statement for asexual reproduction in plants.

options.text: It occurs rapidly during unfavourable conditions.
It involves male and female flowers.
It is found in both lower and higher plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is found in both lower and higher plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** in plants is a process by which new individuals are produced from a **single parent** without the involvement of **gamete formation** or fusion.
 
• **Statement 1**: It occurs rapidly during **unfavourable conditions**. Asexual reproduction typically occurs when environmental conditions are **favourable** and stable, allowing the plant to colonize an area quickly. During **unfavourable conditions**, many plants prefer **sexual reproduction** or produce dormant structures like seeds or spores to ensure survival. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2**: It involves **male and female flowers**. Flowers are the reproductive organs specifically designed for **sexual reproduction**, involving **pollination** and **fertilization**. Asexual reproduction bypasses the floral mechanism entirely. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3**: It is found in both **lower and higher plants**. This is the defining characteristic. **Lower plants** like **Algae**, **Fungi**, and **Bryophytes** reproduce asexually through **fragmentation**, **budding**, or **zoospores**. **Higher plants** (Angiosperms) frequently reproduce asexually through **vegetative propagation** using roots, stems, or leaves. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 4**: It involves **formation of gametes**. The formation and subsequent fusion of **haploid gametes** (sperm and egg) is the hallmark of **sexual reproduction**. Asexual methods rely on **mitotic division** of somatic cells. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vegetative Propagation in Higher Plants**:
 
 
• This is a form of **asexual reproduction** where new plants are produced from vegetative parts.
 
• **Stem Tubers**: Examples include the **Potato**, where "eyes" act as nodes for new growth.
 
• **Rhizomes**: Underground stems found in **Ginger** and **Turmeric** that spread horizontally.
 
• **Runners/Stolons**: Found in **Strawberry** plants, these stems run along the ground to establish new plantlets.
 
• **Bulbs**: Short underground stems with fleshy leaves, such as in **Onions** and **Garlic**.
 
• **Adventitious Buds**: The **Bryophyllum** plant produces buds along its leaf margins that drop off to form new plants.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Methods in Lower Plants**:
 
 
• **Fragmentation**: In **Spirogyra** (an alga), the parent body breaks into smaller pieces, each growing into a new individual.
 
• **Budding**: Common in **Yeast**, where a small bulb-like projection (bud) develops and detaches.
 
• **Spore Formation**: Non-flowering plants like **Ferns** and **Mosses** produce **spores** in structures called **sporangia** which germinate under suitable conditions.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Asexual Reproduction**:
 
 
• The offspring are **genetically identical** (clones) to the parent, ensuring the preservation of **desirable traits**.
 
• It is a **faster** and more **energy-efficient** process as it does not require the plant to produce flowers, nectar, or find pollinators.
 
• It allows for the rapid **multiplication** of a species in a stable habitat.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true for a domestic circuit?

(i) All the appliances are connected in parallel.
(ii) The live wire in the domestic circuit has green insulation on it.
(iii) A fuse connected to the circuit allows excessive current to pass through the appliances.
(iv) The neutral wire in the domestic circuits has black insulation on it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **domestic electric circuit**, all electrical appliances like bulbs, fans, and sockets are connected in **parallel**. This configuration ensures that every appliance receives the same **voltage (220 V in India)** and can be operated independently using its own switch. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• The **live wire** (also known as the phase wire) is the wire through which current enters the circuit and is usually color-coded with **red or brown** insulation. The **green** insulation is strictly reserved for the **earth wire**, which serves as a safety mechanism. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***
 
• An **electric fuse** is a vital safety device designed to **protect appliances**. It consists of a wire with a **low melting point**; if the current becomes **excessive** (due to short-circuiting or overloading), the fuse wire melts and **breaks the circuit** to stop the flow of electricity. ***Hence, statement (iii) is incorrect.***
 
• The **neutral wire** completes the electrical circuit by providing a return path for the current and is maintained at near-zero potential. In standard domestic wiring, the neutral wire is covered with **black or blue** insulation. ***Hence, statement (iv) is correct.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct statements regarding domestic circuits are (i) and (iv).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Standard Voltage and Frequency**: In **India**, the domestic power supply is **Alternating Current (AC)** with a **potential difference of 220 V** and a **frequency of 50 Hz**. This means the direction of current changes **100 times per second**.
 
• **Earthing System**: The **earth wire** (green insulation) is connected to a **metal plate** buried deep in the ground. It is used as a safety measure for appliances with **metallic bodies** (like refrigerators or toasters) to ensure that any leakage of current is transferred safely to the ground, preventing **electric shocks**.
 
• **Short-Circuiting**: This phenomenon occurs when the **live wire** and **neutral wire** come into direct contact. This leads to a massive decrease in resistance and a **sudden surge in current**, which can cause sparks or fires.
 
• **Overloading**: **Overloading** happens when the total power rating of appliances connected to a single circuit exceeds the **current-carrying capacity** of the wires. This usually occurs when too many high-power devices are plugged into one socket.
 
• **MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker)**: In modern domestic circuits, **MCBs** are often used instead of traditional fuses. They automatically **switch off** the electrical supply during an **overload** or **short circuit** and can be easily reset manually once the fault is fixed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Parallel vs. Series**: Domestic circuits never use **series connections** for appliances because in a series circuit, if one appliance fails or is switched off, the **entire circuit breaks** and all other appliances stop working. Furthermore, the **voltage** would be divided among the appliances, causing them to function inefficiently.
 
• **Wire Color Coding**: According to the **new international convention**, the **Live wire** is **Brown**, the **Neutral wire** is **Light Blue**, and the **Earth wire** is **Green or Yellow**. However, the traditional Indian coding of **Red (Live)**, **Black (Neutral)**, and **Green (Earth)** is still widely recognized.
 
• **Two Separate Circuits**: Domestic wiring usually consists of **two separate circuits**: a **5 A** circuit for low-power devices (bulbs, fans) and a **15 A** circuit for high-power devices (geysers, air conditioners).
</ul

questions.question:
Read the given assertion (A) and reason (R) and select the most appropriate option.

**(A): **The onset of puberty in females occurs earlier than in males, but both attain their final height by 18–20 years of age.
**(R):** Although puberty begins later in males, their growth spurt is more rapid than in females.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that the onset of **puberty** in **females** occurs earlier than in **males**. Biologically, **girls** typically enter **puberty** between the **ages of 8 and 13**, while **boys** usually begin between **9 and 14 years**. Despite the difference in start times, both genders generally attain their **final adult height** by the **age of 18–20 years** when the **growth plates** fuse. ***Hence, statement (A) is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** mentions that the **growth spurt** in **males** is more rapid. During the peak of **adolescence**, **males** experience a more intense **height velocity** (approximately **9.5 cm per year**) compared to **females** (approximately **8.3 cm per year**). ***Hence, statement (R) is correct.***
 
• While both statements are factually accurate, the **rapidity** of the **male growth spurt** does not explain **why** **females** start **puberty** earlier or why both finish growing by **age 20**. The timing of **puberty** is controlled by **hormonal signals** from the **hypothalamus**, while the cessation of growth is due to the **fusion** of **epiphyseal plates** caused by **sex steroids**.
 
• Therefore, **Reason (R)** is a true biological fact but it does not serve as a logical explanation for the specific timings mentioned in **Assertion (A)**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Puberty and Hormones**: 
 
 
• In **females**, the primary hormone responsible for **pubertal changes** and eventually the **closure of growth plates** is **Estrogen**.
 
• In **males**, **Testosterone** drives the **growth spurt** and the development of **secondary sexual characteristics** like facial hair and deepening of the voice.
 
 
 
• **Growth Plates (Epiphyseal Plates)**:
 
 
• These are areas of **active cartilage** at the ends of **long bones**. **Height** increases as long as these plates stay open.
 
• By the end of **adolescence** (usually by **age 18-20**), **hormonal changes** cause these plates to **calcify** and turn into bone, marking the end of **vertical growth**.
 
 
 
• **Peak Height Velocity (PHV)**:
 
 
• This refers to the period where the **maximum rate of growth** occurs. **Females** typically reach **PHV** about **two years earlier** than **males**, often around **age 11-12**, whereas **males** reach it around **age 13-14**.
 
• Because **males** have **two additional years** of **pre-pubertal growth** and a more **vigorous growth spurt**, they generally end up taller than **females** on average.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Individual Variation**: While the standard range is **18-20 years**, factors like **nutrition**, **genetics**, and **health conditions** can influence the exact **age** at which an individual stops growing.
 
• **Sexual Dimorphism**: The differences in **growth timing** and **intensity** contribute significantly to **sexual dimorphism** (physical differences between **males** and **females** of the same species) in **human height** and **skeletal structure**.

questions.question: If a cell lacks a functional Golgi complex, it would mainly fail in __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**packaging and secretion**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Golgi complex**, also known as the **Golgi apparatus** or **Golgi body**, is a vital organelle in **eukaryotic cells** responsible for the **modification, sorting, and packaging** of proteins and lipids. 
• Its primary function is to act as a **packaging center**. It receives materials synthesized in the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**, processes them, and then directs them to their final destinations, such as the **plasma membrane** or **lysosomes**. 
• If a cell lacks a functional **Golgi complex**, the proteins and lipids synthesized by the cell would not be **packaged** into vesicles or **secreted** properly. This would lead to a failure in delivering essential molecules to where they are needed inside or outside the cell. ***Hence, the option packaging and secretion is correct.*** 
• The organelle is composed of stacked, flattened, membrane-bound sacs called **cisternae**. These structures are involved in **glycosylation** (adding sugar chains to proteins) and the formation of **glycoproteins** and **glycolipids**. 
• The **Golgi complex** is also essential for the formation of **lysosomes** and the **acrosome** in **sperm cells**, which is necessary for fertilization. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Protein Synthesis:** 
• **Protein synthesis** is primarily the function of **ribosomes** and the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**. 
• While the **Golgi complex** modifies proteins after they are made, it does not actually synthesize them. Therefore, a lack of Golgi would not stop the synthesis of proteins, only their transport and final processing. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*** 
• **Controlling Cell Division:** 
• The regulation and control of **cell division** are managed by the **nucleus** (which contains DNA) and structures like **centrioles** in animal cells. 
• The **Golgi complex** is not the primary controller of the **cell cycle** or **mitosis**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*** 
• **Formation of ATP:** 
• The **formation of ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate) occurs through **cellular respiration** in the **mitochondria**. 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the **powerhouse of the cell**. The **Golgi complex** does not produce energy for the cell. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*** 
• **Discovery:** 
• The **Golgi complex** was discovered by the Italian biologist **Camillo Golgi** in **1898**. He used a specialized silver staining technique called the **black reaction** to identify the organelle's structure. 
• His work on the **nervous system** and the discovery of this organelle earned him the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** in **1906**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Vesicular Transport:** The **Golgi complex** functions by receiving **transport vesicles** from the ER at its **cis face** and releasing secretory vesicles from its **trans face**. 
• **Plant Cells:** In plant cells, the **Golgi apparatus** is often referred to as **dictyosomes**, which are smaller and more scattered compared to animal cells. They play a major role in synthesizing **hemicellulose** and **pectin** for the **cell wall**. 
• **Secretion:** Cells that are highly active in **secretion** (like **pancreatic cells** secreting enzymes or **goblet cells** secreting mucus) have a very high number of **Golgi complexes**. </ul

questions.question: Stars appear to twinkle in the night sky because ______.

options.text: Light from stars undergoes atmospheric refraction
The distance between stars and Earth keeps varying
Stars move rapidly in the sky

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Light from stars undergoes atmospheric refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The twinkling of a star is due to the **atmospheric refraction** of star light. As the light from a star enters the **Earth’s atmosphere**, it undergoes **refraction** continuously before it reaches the **Earth**.
 
• Since the stars are very distant, they approximate **point-sized sources** of light. As the path of rays of light coming from the star goes on varying slightly, the **apparent position** of the star fluctuates and the amount of **starlight** entering the eye flickers. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **atmospheric refraction** occurs in a medium of gradually changing **refractive index**. The **Earth’s atmosphere** is not stationary; its **density** and **temperature** change continuously, leading to changes in the **refractive index** of different layers of air.
 
• While stars may have intrinsic variability, the "twinkling" we observe is primarily an **optical illusion** caused by the atmosphere rather than the stars changing their **brightness** continuously. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **distance** between stars and Earth is vast, and any minor **orbital movement** or **variation in distance** is too insignificant to cause the rapid flickering effect known as twinkling. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Although stars do move at high **velocities**, their **proper motion** is not perceivable over short timeframes to the naked eye and does not cause the twinkling effect. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Why Planets do not Twinkle:** 
 
 
• Unlike stars, **planets** are much closer to the **Earth** and are thus seen as **extended sources** (a collection of many point-sized sources) rather than a single **point source**.
 
• The total variation in the amount of light entering our eye from all the individual **point-sized sources** in a planet will average out to **zero**, thereby **nullifying** the twinkling effect.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction Phenomena:**
 
 
• **Advance Sunrise and Delayed Sunset:** The **Sun** is visible to us about **2 minutes** before the actual sunrise and about **2 minutes** after the actual sunset because of **atmospheric refraction**.
 
• **Apparent Position:** Due to the bending of light, stars appear slightly **higher** (above their actual position) when viewed near the **horizon**.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:** The **refractive index** of the atmosphere generally increases as we move closer to the **Earth's surface** because the air becomes **denser**. This causes the light to bend toward the **normal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scintillation:** This is the scientific term for the **twinkling** of stars. It is caused by **small-scale fluctuations** in the **air density** resulting from **turbulence** in the **atmosphere**.
 
• **Astronomy:** To avoid the blurring and twinkling caused by the **atmosphere**, modern large **telescopes** (like the **Hubble Space Telescope**) are placed in **outer space**, or use **adaptive optics** to cancel out the atmospheric distortion.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct unit for measuring the work done by a force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work** is said to be done when a **force** acts upon an object to cause a **displacement**. The mathematical expression for work done is **W = F × s × cosθ**, where **F** is the force, **s** is the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**. It is named in honor of the **English physicist James Prescott Joule**, who studied the nature of heat and its relationship to mechanical work in the **mid-19th century**.
 
• One **Joule** is defined as the amount of **work done** when a constant **force** of **one Newton** displaces an object through a distance of **one meter** in the direction of the force. Mathematically, **1 J = 1 N · m**.
 
• **Work** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only **magnitude** and no **direction**, even though the force and displacement used to calculate it are **vector quantities**.
 
• In the **CGS (Centimetre-Gram-Second)** system, the unit of work is the **Erg**. The relationship between the two is that **1 Joule** is equal to **10⁷ Ergs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pascal (Pa):**
 
 
• The **Pascal** is the **SI derived unit** of **pressure**. It is defined as **one Newton per square meter (N/m²)**.
 
• It was named after the **French polymath Blaise Pascal** in **1971**. It is commonly used in **meteorology** to measure atmospheric pressure and in **engineering** for material strength.
 
 
 
• **Newton (N):**
 
 
• The **Newton** is the **SI unit** of **force**. It is defined as the force needed to accelerate **one kilogram** of mass at the rate of **one meter per second squared (1 kg·m/s²)**.
 
• Named after **Sir Isaac Newton** in recognition of his work on **classical mechanics** and the **laws of motion** published in **1687**.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb (C):**
 
 
• The **Coulomb** is the **SI unit** of **electric charge**. It is the quantity of electricity transported in **one second** by a current of **one ampere**.
 
• It is named after **Charles-Augustin de Coulomb**, a **French physicist** known for **Coulomb's Law**, which describes the electrostatic force between charges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **dimensional formula** for **Work** is **[ML²T⁻²]**, which is the same as the dimensions for **energy** and **torque**.
 
• Work done can be **positive**, **negative**, or **zero** depending on the angle **θ**. If the force and displacement are in the same direction (**θ = 0°**), work is positive. If they are in opposite directions (**θ = 180°**), work is negative.
 
• **Zero Work:** No work is done if the **displacement** is **zero**, or if the force is **perpendicular** to the displacement (**θ = 90°**), such as a person carrying a load on their head while walking horizontally.
 
• In **atomic physics**, work and energy are often measured in a smaller unit called the **electronvolt (eV)**, where **1 eV ≈ 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ Joules**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the characteristic property of a non-metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poor conductor of electricity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-metals** are elements that generally lack the characteristics of metals. One of their most defining physical properties is that they are **poor conductors of electricity** and **heat**. This is because non-metals do not have **free-moving electrons** (delocalized electrons) in their structure to carry an electric charge.
 
• Most **non-metals** have **low melting points** and **low boiling points** compared to metals. This is due to the weak **intermolecular forces** (like Van der Waals forces) that hold their molecules together, which require less energy to overcome.
 
• **Non-metals** are **brittle** in their solid state. Unlike metals, they cannot be beaten into thin sheets (**malleability**) or drawn into wires (**ductility**). If subjected to stress, they tend to shatter or break into pieces.
 
• They are **non-sonorous**, meaning they do not produce a deep, ringing sound when struck. This is a sharp contrast to metals, which are used in bells and musical instruments for their **sonorous** property.
 
• In terms of chemical behavior, non-metals are **electronegative**. They have a tendency to **gain electrons** during chemical reactions to form **negative ions** (anions) or share electrons to form **covalent bonds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical State**: Unlike metals, which are mostly solids at **room temperature**, non-metals can exist in all three states of matter. For example, **Oxygen** and **Nitrogen** are gases, **Carbon** and **Sulfur** are solids, and **Bromine** is the only non-metal that is a **liquid** at room temperature.
 
• **Lustre**: Non-metals generally have a **dull appearance** and do not reflect light well (they are **non-lustrous**). However, **Iodine** and **Graphite** are notable exceptions as they exhibit a metallic-like shine or lustre.
 
• **Exceptions to Conductivity**: While non-metals are typically insulators, **Graphite** (an allotrope of **Carbon**) is a **good conductor of electricity**. This unique property allows it to be used in **electrodes** and **dry cells**.
 
• **Hardness**: Most non-metals are relatively soft compared to metals. However, **Diamond** (another allotrope of **Carbon**) is the **hardest known natural substance** and has an extremely **high melting point**.
 
• **Oxides**: Non-metals react with **oxygen** to form **acidic or neutral oxides**. For instance, **Sulfur dioxide (SO2)** is acidic, whereas **Carbon monoxide (CO)** and **Water (H2O)** are neutral oxides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ductility**: This is a property of **metals** (like **Gold** and **Copper**) that allows them to be drawn into thin wires. Non-metals lack this property.
 
• **Density**: Non-metals usually have **low densities** and are lighter than metals. They do not have the high mass-to-volume ratio characteristic of transition metals.
 
• **Valence Electrons**: Non-metals generally have **4 to 8 electrons** in their **outermost shell**. This configuration drives their reactivity toward gaining electrons to achieve a stable **noble gas configuration**.
 
• **Uses**: Non-metals are essential for life. **Oxygen** is vital for respiration, **Nitrogen** is used in fertilizers, **Chlorine** is used for water purification, and **Phosphorus** is used in matchsticks.
</ul

questions.question: For spherical mirrors of small apertures, the relation between the radius of curvature (R) and focal length (f) is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R = 2f**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A spherical mirror is a mirror whose reflecting surface is a part of a hollow sphere of glass. The center of this sphere is known as the **Center of Curvature (C)**.
 
• The **Radius of Curvature (R)** is defined as the distance between the **Pole (P)** of the mirror and the **Center of Curvature (C)**.
 
• The **Principal Focus (F)** is a point on the principal axis where all rays parallel to the axis converge (in a concave mirror) or appear to diverge from (in a convex mirror) after reflection.
 
• The **Focal Length (f)** is the distance from the **Pole (P)** to the **Principal Focus (F)**.
 
• For spherical mirrors with a **small aperture**, the **Principal Focus (F)** lies exactly at the midpoint of the distance between the **Pole (P)** and the **Center of Curvature (C)**.
 
• Because the focus is the midpoint, the **Radius of Curvature (R)** is twice the **Focal Length (f)**. Mathematically, this is expressed as **R = 2f**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:** This is a **converging mirror** where the reflecting surface is curved inwards. Its focal length is considered **negative** in the standard Cartesian sign convention. It is commonly used in **solar cookers**, **torches**, and by **dentists** to see larger images of teeth.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** This is a **diverging mirror** where the reflecting surface is curved outwards. Its focal length is considered **positive**. These mirrors are primarily used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they provide a wider **field of view** and always form an **erect, virtual, and diminished image**.
 
• **Aperture:** The **aperture** of a spherical mirror is the diameter of its reflecting surface. It represents the size of the mirror that faces the incident light.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the pole is treated as the origin. Distances measured in the direction of incident light are **positive**, while those measured against the direction of incident light are **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The relationship **R = 2f** is only strictly accurate for **paraxial rays**. These are rays that strike the mirror very close to the **Pole (P)** and make small angles with the principal axis.
 
• If the **aperture** of the mirror is large, rays falling near the edges of the mirror (marginal rays) do not meet at the same focal point as the paraxial rays. This defect in image formation is known as **spherical aberration**.
 
• The **Mirror Formula**, which relates focal length, object distance (u), and image distance (v), is given by **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**. This formula is derived using the **R = 2f** assumption for small apertures.
 
• In **year 1672**, **Isaac Newton** used the properties of spherical and parabolic mirrors to construct the first reflecting telescope, significantly advancing the field of **optics**.
</ul

questions.question: The right-hand thumb rule is used to find which of the following?

options.text: Direction of force on a current-carrying conductor
Direction of magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Direction of magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right-hand thumb rule**, often attributed to **Maxwell**, is a fundamental principle in **electromagnetism** used to determine the **direction of magnetic field lines** produced by a **straight current-carrying conductor**.
 
• According to this rule, if a **current-carrying conductor** is held in the **right hand** such that the **thumb points** in the **direction of the electric current**, then the **fingers** will **curl** around the conductor in the **direction of the magnetic field lines**.
 
• This rule visualizes the **magnetic field** as **concentric circles** surrounding the wire. If the **current** flows **upwards**, the **magnetic field** moves in an **anticlockwise direction** (when viewed from above). *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• The **Right-hand thumb rule** does not determine the **magnitude of the current**; the magnitude is usually measured using an **ammeter** in **Amperes (A)**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• The **direction of force** on a conductor is determined by **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**, not the thumb rule. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The **resistance of a wire** is a property of the material and its dimensions, calculated using **Ohm's Law (V=IR)** or the **resistivity formula**, and is independent of the thumb rule. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maxwell’s Corkscrew Rule**: 
 
 
• This is another version of the **Right-hand thumb rule**. It states that if a **right-handed corkscrew** is rotated such that it moves in the **direction of the current**, the **direction of rotation** represents the **direction of the magnetic field**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Properties**:
 
 
• The **strength of the magnetic field** (B) produced by a straight wire is **directly proportional** to the **magnitude of the current** (I) and **inversely proportional** to the **distance** (r) from the wire.
 
• The **S.I. unit** of the **magnetic field** is the **Tesla (T)**.
 
 
 
• **Circular Loops and Solenoids**:
 
 
• The **Right-hand thumb rule** is also applicable to **circular loops**. If the **fingers** curl in the **direction of the current** in the loop, the **thumb points** in the **direction of the magnetic field** at the **center of the loop**.
 
• In a **solenoid**, this rule helps identify the **North and South poles** created by the flow of electricity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**: Specifically used for **Electric Motors**. The **thumb** indicates **Motion/Force**, the **forefinger** indicates the **Magnetic Field**, and the **middle finger** indicates the **Current**.
 
• **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule**: Specifically used for **Electric Generators** to find the **direction of induced current**. The **thumb** indicates the **motion of the conductor**, the **forefinger** indicates the **magnetic field**, and the **middle finger** indicates the **induced current**.
 
• **Discovery**: The relationship between **electricity and magnetism** was first observed by **Hans Christian Oersted** in **1820**, when he noticed a **compass needle** deflect near a wire carrying **electric current**.
 
• **Applications**: Understanding these rules is essential for the **design and functioning** of **electromagnets**, **transformers**, **speakers**, and various **industrial sensors**.

questions.question: According to Bohr's model, electromagnetic radiations possess dual character properties behaving like:
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**waves and particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **dual character** of electromagnetic radiation means that it exhibits both **wave-like** and **particle-like** properties. This concept was fundamental in the transition from classical physics to **quantum mechanics**.
 
• The **wave nature** is evidenced by phenomena such as **interference** and **diffraction**. These properties suggest that radiation travels through space as oscillating electric and magnetic fields. ***Hence, the first part of the option is correct.***
 
• The **particle nature** (also known as the corpuscular nature) is demonstrated through **Black Body Radiation** and the **Photoelectric Effect**. These phenomena could not be explained by classical wave theory and required the concept of discrete energy packets. ***Hence, the second part of the option is correct.***
 
• **Niels Bohr** incorporated these dualistic ideas into his **1913 Atomic Model**. He proposed that **electrons** move in fixed orbits and that the **energy** emitted or absorbed during transitions between these orbits occurs in discrete units or **photons**, which aligns with the particle theory.
 
• By accepting that light behaves as both **waves and particles**, scientists were able to resolve the inconsistencies between the **continuous spectra** predicted by classical physics and the **line spectra** observed in elements like **hydrogen**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Quantum Theory of Radiation:**
 
 
• **Max Planck** proposed in **1900** that atoms and molecules could emit or absorb energy only in discrete quantities called **quanta**. The energy of a quantum is proportional to its frequency.
 
• The relationship is given by the equation **E = hν**, where **h** is **Planck’s constant**, valued at approximately **6.626 x 10⁻³⁴ Joules-second (J·s)**.
 
 
 
• **The Photoelectric Effect:**
 
 
• In **1905**, **Albert Einstein** applied **Planck's** theory to light, suggesting that light itself consists of particles called **photons**. 
 
• This discovery provided the strongest evidence for the **particle nature** of electromagnetic radiation and earned **Einstein** the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1921**.
 
 
 
• **Wave Nature of Light:**
 
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell** established in the **1860s** that light is an **electromagnetic wave** traveling at a constant speed of **3 x 10⁸ meters per second** in a vacuum.
 
• Characteristics of these waves include **wavelength (λ)** and **frequency (ν)**, related by the formula **c = λν**.
 
 
 
• **De Broglie Hypothesis:**
 
 
• In **1924**, **Louis de Broglie** extended the dual nature of light to all matter, proposing that particles like **electrons** also possess **wave-like** characteristics, a concept known as **matter waves**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Photons:**
 
 
• A **photon** has **zero rest mass** but possesses **momentum** and **energy**. This allows it to exert pressure, known as **radiation pressure**.
 
• The energy of a photon is directly proportional to its **frequency** and inversely proportional to its **wavelength**.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Spectrum:**
 
 
• The spectrum includes **Gamma rays**, **X-rays**, **Ultraviolet**, **Visible light**, **Infrared**, **Microwaves**, and **Radio waves**. High-frequency waves like **Gamma rays** exhibit more pronounced **particle-like** behavior.
 
• Low-frequency radiations like **Radio waves** exhibit more pronounced **wave-like** behavior, making them ideal for communication over long distances.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about an unbalanced force acting on an object?

options.text: It brings the object in motion.
It has no effect on the object’s state of motion.
It keeps the object at rest.
It always increases the mass of the object.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It brings the object in motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **unbalanced force** is defined as a force where the **net resultant force** acting on an object is **not zero**. When multiple forces act on a body and do not cancel each other out, the object experiences a change in its **state of motion**.
 
• According to **Newton’s First Law of Motion**, an object will maintain its **state of rest** or **uniform motion** in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by an **external unbalanced force**.
 
• **Statement 1**: "It brings the object in motion." If an unbalanced force is applied to a stationary object, it overcomes the object's **inertia** and causes it to start moving in the direction of the **resultant force**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2**: "It has no effect on the object’s state of motion." This description applies to **balanced forces**, where the forces are equal in **magnitude** but opposite in **direction**, resulting in a **net force** of **zero**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3**: "It keeps the object at rest." An unbalanced force, by definition, causes **acceleration**. If an object remains at rest despite forces being applied, it means the forces are **balanced** (such as static friction balancing a push). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: "It always increases the mass of the object." **Mass** is an intrinsic property representing the amount of matter in an object and its **inertia**. In classical mechanics, applying a **force** does not change the **mass** of the object. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**: This law provides a quantitative definition of force, stating that the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the **net force** acting on it and inversely proportional to its **mass**. The relationship is expressed by the formula **F = ma**.
 
• **Acceleration and Velocity**: An unbalanced force always results in **acceleration**, which means a change in the **velocity** of the object. This can involve an increase in speed, a decrease in speed (**deceleration**), or a change in the **direction** of motion.
 
• **Vector Nature of Force**: **Force** is a **vector quantity**, characterized by both **magnitude** and **direction**. The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**, named after **Sir Isaac Newton** for his work on classical mechanics in **1687**.
 
• **Inertia**: This is the tendency of objects to resist any change in their state of motion. The **mass** of an object is a measure of its **inertia**; a heavier object requires a larger **unbalanced force** to achieve the same **acceleration** as a lighter object.
 
• **Types of Forces**: Forces can be categorized into **contact forces** (like friction, tension, and normal force) and **non-contact forces** (like **gravitational force**, **magnetic force**, and **electrostatic force**). Any of these can act as an **unbalanced force** depending on the system.

questions.question: The unicellular organism amoeba has a __________ shape.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**changing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An **Amoeba** is a **unicellular organism** that belongs to the **Kingdom Protista** and is characterized by its **lack of a definite shape**.
 
• The shape of an amoeba is **constantly changing** because of the movement of its **cytoplasm** and the formation of **pseudopodia**.
 
• **Pseudopodia**, which literally means "**false feet**," are temporary **protrusions** of the **cell membrane** that the organism extends and pulls back to facilitate **locomotion**.
 
• In addition to movement, these **pseudopodia** are used for **capturing food** through a process known as **phagocytosis**, where the organism wraps its body around a food particle to form a **food vacuole**.
 
• Because it lacks a **cell wall** or a **pellicle** (a stiff outer covering found in some other protists), the amoeba remains **irregular** and **flexible** throughout its life cycle.

questions.question: Where is a reflex arc formed in the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spinal cord**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **reflex arc** is a neural pathway that controls a **reflex action**. In higher animals, most sensory neurons do not pass directly into the brain, but synapse in the **spinal cord**.
 
• The **reflex arc** is formed in the **spinal cord** to allow for faster **reflex actions** by activating spinal motor neurons without the delay of routing signals through the brain.
 
• While the information input also goes on to reach the brain, the immediate response is coordinated by the **spinal cord** to ensure a quick reaction to potentially harmful stimuli.
 
• The process starts when a **receptor** detects a stimulus; the signal then travels through a **sensory neuron** to the **spinal cord**, where it is processed by an **interneuron** (in polysynaptic reflexes) and sent back via a **motor neuron** to an **effector**.
 
• This mechanism is an **evolutionary adaptation** that helps organisms survive by responding nearly instantaneously to environmental hazards, such as heat or sharp objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of a Reflex Arc**:
 
 
• **Receptor**: The specialized cell or organ that perceives the stimulus (e.g., **skin**).
 
• **Sensory Neuron**: Carries the impulse from the receptor to the **Central Nervous System (CNS)**.
 
• **Integration Center**: Located within the **spinal cord**, where the sensory impulse is converted into a motor impulse.
 
• **Motor Neuron**: Transmits the impulse from the **spinal cord** to the **effector organ**.
 
• **Effector**: The **muscle** or gland that responds to the motor impulse.
 
 
 
• **Forebrain**:
 
 
• The **Forebrain** is the main thinking part of the brain. It consists of the **cerebrum**, **thalamus**, and **hypothalamus**.
 
• It deals with **voluntary actions**, memory, learning, and the processing of sensory information like sight and sound.
 
 
 
• **Hindbrain**:
 
 
• The **Hindbrain** consists of the **pons**, **cerebellum**, and **medulla**.
 
• It controls **involuntary actions** such as blood pressure, salivation, and vomiting, and coordinates body posture and balance.
 
 
 
• **Muscle (The Effector)**:
 
 
• In the context of a reflex arc, the **muscle** acts as the **effector** that performs the physical movement (contraction) to pull away from a stimulus.
 
 
 
• **Types of Reflexes**:
 
 
• **Spinal Reflexes**: Reflexes where the **spinal cord** is the primary control center (e.g., the **knee-jerk reflex**).
 
• **Cranial Reflexes**: Reflexes where the **brain** is the control center (e.g., **blinking** of eyes in response to bright light).

questions.question: What is the mass number of an element defined as?

options.text: Sum of the number of protons and neutrons
Sum of the number of electrons and protons

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sum of the number of protons and neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **mass number** (represented by the symbol **A**) of an element is defined as the total **sum of the number of protons and neutrons** present in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• Protons and neutrons are collectively known as **nucleons** because they are situated in the **nucleus** of the atom.
 
• The relationship between the mass number and the identity of an atom is expressed by the formula: **Mass Number (A) = Atomic Number (Z) + Number of Neutrons (n)**.
 
• While the **atomic number** identifies the number of protons (and thus the element itself), the **mass number** accounts for the bulk of the atom's physical mass.
 
• Since the mass of an **electron** is approximately **1/1840th** of the mass of a proton, it is considered negligible and is not included when calculating the **mass number**. Hence, the correct answer is the sum of protons and neutrons.</str

questions.question: The stethoscope works on which principle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multiple reflection of sound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **stethoscope** is an essential medical instrument used by healthcare professionals to listen to the **internal sounds** of an animal or human body, primarily those originating from the **heart** or **lungs**.
 
• It functions based on the principle of **multiple reflection of sound**. When the **diaphragm** of the stethoscope is placed on the patient's chest, the internal sounds (like heartbeats) create vibrations that turn into **longitudinal sound waves**.
 
• These sound waves pass through the **hollow plastic or rubber tubes** of the stethoscope. Inside these tubes, the sound waves strike the inner walls and undergo **repeated reflections** (multiple reflections) before reaching the doctor's ears.
 
• This process of **multiple reflection** ensures that the sound energy is confined within the tube and directed toward the ear tips without significant loss of intensity, allowing the doctor to hear even faint sounds clearly.
 
• The **chest piece** usually contains a **diaphragm** and a **bell**. The diaphragm is designed to capture **high-frequency** sounds, while the bell is used for **low-frequency** sounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refraction of Sound:** This is the **bending** of sound waves when they pass from one medium to another with a different **density** or temperature. While sound refracts in the atmosphere, it is not the mechanism used in a stethoscope.
 
• **Diffraction of Sound:** This refers to the **spreading out** or bending of sound waves around obstacles or through narrow openings. While sound waves naturally diffract, this property is not utilized for the amplification or transmission of sound in medical auscultation devices.
 
• **Dispersion of Sound:** This is the phenomenon where sound waves of different **frequencies** travel at different speeds, causing a pulse to spread out. This is generally not a factor in the functional design of a standard acoustic stethoscope.
 
• **Invention:** The stethoscope was invented in **France** in **1816** by **René Laennec**. The original version was a simple **wooden tube**, which was far more effective and hygienic than the previous method of placing the ear directly on the patient's chest.
 
• **Acoustic vs. Electronic:** While traditional **acoustic stethoscopes** rely entirely on **physical reflection**, modern **electronic stethoscopes** amplify the sound electronically and can even convert the acoustic sound into digital data for further analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reflection Laws:** The reflection of sound follows the same laws as the reflection of light: the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection**, and the incident wave, reflected wave, and the normal all lie in the **same plane**.
 
• **Sound Propagation:** Sound requires a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. In a stethoscope, the sound travels through the **air column** inside the tubing, reflecting off the solid walls of the tube.
 
• **Applications:** Beyond the heart and lungs, stethoscopes are used to listen to the **intestines** (bowel sounds) and **blood flow** in arteries and veins (especially during blood pressure measurement using a **sphygmomanometer**).
 
• **Design Features:** The **tubing** length is usually between **18 to 27 inches**. Shorter tubing may provide better sound quality but requires the doctor to be closer to the patient. The material is typically **PVC**, which provides the necessary flexibility and internal smoothness for **efficient reflection**.
